## Current focus

1.3.0 (unreleased, branch `update/1.3.0`) replaces the forge and anvil minigames with hands-on, in-world work: plan
`docs/plans/2026-11-13-cinematic-overhaul-plan.md`, evidence and migration notes in `docs/cinematic-overhaul/`.
Domain rules and server services are in `work/` (`ThermalRules`, `ShapingRules`, `QuenchRules`, `WorkQuality`,
`ProcessState`, `ProcessProfiles`, `ForgeJob`, `WorkLeases`, `SmithingActionService`, `Forge/Anvil/Trough/GrindstoneActions`,
`SmithingCompletionService`); the client is `client/work/` (`FocusController`, `WorkCamera` + `mixin/client/CameraMixin`,
`WorkFocusScreen`, `WorkTargets`, `WorkHud`, `WorldViewInput`, `WorkpieceShape/Renderer`, `SceneTools`, `WorkEffects`).
13 process profiles (data) and 13 workpiece profiles (assets) cover the 44 anvil patterns. The pack-test `SmithDriver`
plays a whole piece through real client inputs (smoke test, store screenshots, showcase).

1.2.0 had three parts:

- **Epic Fight and Epic Knights.** Curated integrations with bundled data generated by `tools/generate_epic_compat.py`
  (policy in `tools/epic_compat_manifest.py`). Coverage per item: `compat/CoveragePolicies` and `WeaponCatalog`
  dispositions, checked by `CoverageGameTests` against `docs/compatibility/inventory/<profile>/`. See
  `docs/compatibility/epic-integrations.md`.
- **Stations.** Models within budget (`tools/model_preview.py --check`), `StationShape` boxes checked by
  `StationShapeGameTests`, measured by the pack-test `StationBenchmark` (`-PstationBenchmark=<label>`).
- **Forge screen `@mod` search.**

Done in 1.1.x: progression hooks, Simply Swords and the first Epic Fight support, the vanilla GUI
(`docs/vanilla-gui/REVIEW.md`).

Done in 1.0.0, for Ultima:

- pack metals with upgrade policies;
- consumed-equipment auxiliaries and upgrade chains;
- loot quality and the Maker's Mark;
- `ItemSmithedEvent` and the Jade overlays.

Next is in-game playtesting of feel and balance, and the sibling-repo hooks (Runic Skills, Runic Gods, Runic Races) on the new event.

## Decisions

- 1.3.0: progression hooks are consulted where the work is authorised: the recipe gate and cost modifier when a plan
  is pinned (`SessionManager.selectRecipe`) and again at `ForgeActions.commit`, which charges the units and freezes them
  into the `ForgeJob` (so `ItemSmithedEvent.getMetalUnits()` is what was paid); the grindstone cost at
  `GrindstoneActions.finishPass`; `ISmithingAssistSource` (ANVIL only) divides blow recovery in `AnvilActions.recoveryTicks`.
- 1.3.0 is a native Forge adapter, not Diegesis: Diegesis stations own library-persisted slots, it would be a hard runtime
  dependency on a beta library, and it has no Maven artifact (plan, section 2).
- 1.3.0 state: workpiece schema 3 (`Process` compound) with explicit v1/v2 migration and deterministic legacy ids; an
  unreadable record is kept raw in its holder. Heat is integer 0..10000 with per-holder work clocks (no offline or
  unloaded cooling); `StrictMath` keeps client prediction and server results identical.
- 1.3.0 authority: protocol 6. `WorkActionPacket` carries intents only; `SmithingActionService` validates action, finite
  numbers, loaded station and instance id, reach and sight from the real eyes, the `WorkLeases` lease (permission via
  `mayInteract` + `ForgeHooks.onRightClickBlock`), sequence and token budget. Job ownership is a time window
  (`work.jobPrioritySeconds`), never online state, so fake players and offline owners behave the same.
- 1.3.0 input: in `WorkFocusScreen` the work keys are handled before the movement keys, because the default action key
  (Space) is also the default jump key; a key repeat is not another press.
- Smithing recipes are a real `RecipeType` so they live in `data/<ns>/recipes/` (the plan suggested `data/<ns>/immersive_smithing/recipes/`, which the recipe manager would not load). Automatic recipes are inserted into the recipe manager so clients and JEI receive them.
- `SmithingData.rebuild` runs on `ServerStartedEvent` and on `OnDatapackSyncEvent` (player == null), because tags are not bound while reload listeners run and that event fires before the recipe packet.
- Durability quality converts incoming damage (1/multiplier with a stored fractional carry) instead of changing max durability, so arbitrary modded items, Unbreaking and Mending keep working.
- Efficacy adds separate attribute modifiers (fixed UUIDs per slot) next to the item's own; mining speed is multiplied in `BreakSpeed`. Shields are efficacy-neutral.
- Only exact `SmithingTransformRecipe` upgrades are suppressed on the smithing table; trim recipes report a sample chestplate as their result and must never be removed.
- Curated integrations (`compat/Integrations`, `curated = true`: Epic Fight, Epic Knights) are never auto-detected; their
  bundled recipes name their sources in `replaces` / `derived_from` (server-only fields, not synced: no protocol
  change). `SmithingData` drops such a recipe while none of the named recipes is loaded, and suppresses exactly the
  named ones. TerraFirmaCraft is a switch without data: off by default, opting in means automatic detection.
- `material/MaterialDefinition.sourcesOnly` files only add sources (Epic Knights plates); a family made only of them
  is dropped, so a plate never creates its metal.
- `recipe/SourceRecipes` decides what may be adapted at all. These may: exact `ShapedRecipe`, `ShapelessRecipe` and `SmithingTransformRecipe` classes, and the data-carrying serializers listed there (`botania:armor_upgrade`). Any other class or serializer is `CUSTOM`: never converted, never disabled, and reported as kept. That covers subclasses and Simply Swords' `smithing_reroll`.
- Suppression is per source recipe (`SmithingData.replacing` / `replacingUpgrade`). A native recipe is removed only when a forge recipe was generated from it (`sourceRecipe`), or makes the same item from the same metal (for upgrades, the addition's). Everything else goes to `report.retained` with a reason. A crafting recipe that adds no metal to a finished piece is a remake: it is kept, and `QualityInheritance` carries the quality.
- Rebuilds are repeatable. `SmithingData.sourceRecipes` keeps the recipes as the last datapack load produced them (`sourceSnapshot`). It recognises its own previous output by identity (`lastWritten`), so a rebuild never analyses generated recipes or forgets one it removed.
- The repair material decides the primary metal (`AutoRecipeDetector.primaryMaterial`, via `Item#isValidRepairItem`). Fittings of another metal become auxiliaries only while they total fewer units than the primary. A non-metal repair material is `NON_METAL_PRIMARY`, which is skipped.
- Spartan Weaponry support is generated data (`tools/generate_spartan_compat.py`), not code: one explicit recipe per metal and type under `recipes/compat/spartanweaponry/`, conditions ordered `forge:mod_loaded` then Spartan's `type_disabled` (Forge stops at the first false condition, so Spartan's condition type is never parsed without Spartan). Toggle: server config `integrations.spartanWeaponry`.
- A shield ingredient is dismissed (neither cost nor auxiliary) when the result is a shield. Other equipment ingredients follow the finished-piece rules in `generateChains`.
- Smithing-table upgrades are redirected through the public `SmithingTransformRecipe#isBaseIngredient/isAdditionIngredient` (no access transformer); cost = the base item's shape in the addition's metal.
- Projectile quality multiplies `AbstractArrow` base damage once, on first level join (persistent-data flag), from the thrown weapon or the firing bow/crossbow.
- Tongs stab: first person via `IClientItemExtensions#applyForgeHandTransform`, third person via `HumanoidModelMixin` (`require = 0`: cosmetic, must never crash a pack). The shared parent model `models/item/tongs.json` holds the tongs along the arm in third person (hanging at rest), because a normal handheld item points forward and would tip upward as the arm thrusts. A hammer blow's arm swing is started by the client (`SceneTools.strike`) and broadcast by vanilla.
- A committed job's escrow is saved with the job in the forge block entity and refunded once on cancel or break. Escrow
  from a 1.2 minigame session (no job) is loaded as `legacyEscrow` and dropped at the forge on the next tick, once.
- Upgrades into a metal follow that material's `upgrade_policy`: `shape` (the base's shape in the new metal, no base needed; netherite, dragonsteel) or `addition` (the addition plus the consumed base; ignitium, cursium, witherite, pyrium, terrasteel). A base without a metal shape always uses `addition`. Consumed bases are auxiliaries with `consumesEquipment`, matched by item only, so escrow and refund code is unchanged.
- Finished pieces in crafting (`AutoRecipeDetector.generateChains`) are handled after the smithing-table pass, with the same `UpgradeContext`. There are three cases:
  - **Growth:** the same metal; the piece's own recipe plus the added metal, within one `equipmentKind`.
  - **Chain:** another metal, priced like an upgrade. It needs a base of the result's class (`isUpgradeBase`) that the forge already makes.
  - **Remake:** no metal, so the recipe is `NOT_METAL` and kept.
  A final reporting pass gives every skipped piece recipe its reason.
- `AutoRecipeDetector.baseShape` expands a finished piece nested in an upgrade base's recipe, but inside it only gems and ingots count as material slots, never the outer base's repair item. Without that guard, Iron's Botany's manasteel wizard armour (Iron's Spells cloth built on leather armour) was priced as a 36–72 unit manasteel shape, when it should rework its base for one ingot (`addition`). The Ultima release gate caught it, and `RecipePipelineGameTests.clothBasesAreReworkedNotPricedAsMetal` pins it.
- The forged piece is assembled by `ResultAssembler` from the escrow before `completeSession` charges any metal. A failure cancels with a refund. A recipe reworking exactly one piece keeps that piece's tag when `keepsBaseData()` is true, minus the quality root and with the recipe result's own keys on top. `Damage` is never overwritten by the result's `Damage:0`. Automatic recipes take `keep_base_data` from `SourceRecipes.Kind.carriesBaseData`.
- Loot quality is a global loot modifier (`loot/ForgedLootModifier`). It grades what `QualityEligibility` allows: items with a smithing recipe, plus `#immersive_smithing:quality_eligible` while that mod's integration is on. Mob-held equipment drops bypass loot tables and stay ungraded. The grindstone starts an ungraded eligible piece at 50/50 and writes that grade only with a paid refinement.
- Crafting inheritance is server-side in `onItemCrafted`, mirrored for the preview by `mixin/CraftingMenuMixin` (`require = 0`). Smithing-table upgrades and rerolls copy the base's tag natively, so they need no hook.
- Epic Fight and Simply Swords support is data only: shape tags, three patterns, tags, and automatic detection. Main code never references their classes; only the GameTests compile against them (`gameTestCompileOnly`). `compat/Integrations` maps a namespace or recipe id to its toggle (`integrations.epicFight`, `integrations.simplySwords`, plus Spartan and Spartan Fire under `spartanWeaponry`).
- Quality stays in attribute modifiers, so Epic Fight's off-hand swap and Simply Swords' attack-scaled abilities read it exactly once. Simply Swords' thrown entities take damage from the stack at launch and are tagged `weapon_scaled_projectiles` so `ProjectileEfficacy` skips them.
- GameTest support classes for optional mods keep vanilla types in every signature, so their classes resolve only when the mod is loaded: JVM verification loads referenced classes when the caller class is verified.
- Simply Swords and Architectury are built with Architectury Loom: their mixin annotations name SRG members, and there is no refmap. Dev runs with `-PsimplySwords` therefore go through `remapDevMods` (`tools/devmods/remap_srg_strings.py`), which rewrites those strings with `createSrgToMcp`. Production is unaffected.
- The screens draw vanilla textures through `client/screen/VanillaGui`, with fixed vanilla text colours; `gui/smithing.png` keeps only the anvil ring and disc. `WorkshopScreen` scales one canvas of at least 320 x 240, and tooltips are deferred to screen space.
- The pack-test agent's accessibility toggles converge and verify rather than set once. Forge autosaves each option, and its config watcher can reload an older file between quick writes, which once left high contrast on in the dev profile.
- The Maker's Mark lives in the quality compound (`SmithName`, `SmithUUID`, `Signed`); title and inscription are vanilla `display.Name`/`Lore`. Only `SigningService.sign` writes a signature, after checking the slot, the smith and Faulty, and sanitising the strings. The screen opens from `OpenMakersMarkPacket` (which carries the stack, because the inventory sync arrives a tick later).
- `ItemSmithedEvent` is posted before the piece enters the inventory, so listeners can still change the stack. The vanilla `ItemCraftedEvent` is fired with a one-slot container; Runic Skills classifies that as UNKNOWN (no reward) by design, its integration belongs on the new event.
- Jade support is `compat/jade/SmithingJadePlugin`, discovered by `@WailaPlugin`; server data providers write the block entity state so the overlay does not depend on client sync. Dependency `curse.maven:jade-324717:<jade_curse_file>` (compileOnly).
- A block entity's update tag must never be empty: `ClientboundBlockEntityDataPacket` turns an empty tag into null and the client then skips `load`, keeping stale contents (an anvil still showing a workpiece taken with tongs). The anvil always writes `Occupied` and loads even an empty packet; `StationSyncGameTests` replays the real packet into a detached copy for each station. Station messages are `StationNotices` (S2C `StationNoticePacket`), not the action bar.

## Known issues

- Sounds reuse vanilla sound events through `sounds.json`; no custom audio yet.
- Ultima (CurseForge pack) on the NVIDIA GPU under Hyprland/Xwayland: Forge's early loading window fails its hand-off to the game window (reproduced 2/2 without this mod; the user saw a frozen loading screen). Fixed in that instance with `earlyWindowControl = false` in `config/fml.toml` (backup `fml.toml.bak`).
- Ultima renders first person through First-person Model (the body model, not vanilla hands), so there the stab is the third-person pose and `TongsClientExtensions#applyForgeHandTransform` is unused. Its animation mods also raise the free arm during any swing (a plain sword swing does the same; see the pack test's `packtest_sword_third_person.png`).
- The pack-test agent takes Origins' offered choice on first join, and the harness turns off MCA's `launchIntoDestiny` in its copy, so the in-game shots show the staged world.
- Visual assets have editable pixel-art sources in `art/smithing_art.py` and custom Java Block/Item models. `tools/generate_textures.py` verifies by default; only explicit `--write` exports artwork. See `art/README.md`, `docs/visual-overhaul/REPORT.md` (1.0.0, history) and `docs/vanilla-gui/REVIEW.md` (current screens) for source and validation details.
